title: Independent annotated microscopy research capstone
intro: Specify and audit an unfamiliar microscopy problem from first principles, with independent reference annotations, group-safe validation, source integrity, biological endpoints and a defensible go/no-go memo.

scientific_context.caution: Public browser checks do not certify hidden biological ground truth, independent research ability, source-disjointness or exopher identity.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → independent Apply/Prove → capstone evidence checkpoints → delayed independent review and human judgment.

goals.title: Prespecify the biological question and endpoint
goals.why: Segmentation cannot be assessed until the intended biological object and primary measurement are defined.
explain: Nuclei, fluorescent aggregates and exophers are different biological entities.
Prespecify ambiguous and border cases before looking at holdout annotations.
A complete document is necessary but human review must assess whether definitions are biologically appropriate.

goals.title: Freeze a group-disjoint development/test split
goals.why: Training on one field and testing on another from the same animal may overstate generalization.
explain: Split by independent animal, acquisition session or experiment as appropriate.
A sample ID alone does not establish independent biological origin.
Freeze the partition before tuning segmentation hyperparameters.

capstone.title: Independent unfamiliar-dataset evidence audit
capstone.why: The final research decision must integrate source identity, study split, errors, reproducibility and biological interpretation.
